title: AI Reporting Tools: Top 16 Picks I Tested and Ranked in 2026
summary: AI reporting tools split into two camps, BI dashboards and automated report generators. I tested dozens of platforms to find the top 16 for 2026.
body_markdown:
AI reporting tools turn raw data into dashboards, charts, or full reports without hours of manual work.


I ran mock datasets through dozens of platforms and compared setup time, chart quality, and how well each handled a written summary. That testing narrowed the field down to the 16 worth your time.


Here's how each one stacks up, and which fits your workflow.


## 16 best AI reporting tools: TL;DR


1. **[Tableau](https://www.tableau.com/) :** Best for enterprise teams that need deep, interactive data visualization across multiple departments
2. **[Power BI](https://powerbi.microsoft.com/) :** Best for teams already working inside Microsoft 365 who want reporting built into Excel and Teams
3. **[Domo](https://www.domo.com/) :** Best for operations teams that need real-time dashboards pulling from a wide range of connected data sources
4. **[Julius](https://julius.ai/) :** Best for marketers and analysts who want a written report with computed charts built from a spreadsheet or database in one step
5. **[Whatagraph](https://whatagraph.com/) :** Best for marketing agencies generating full client reports from a single text prompt
6. **[Data Studio](https://datastudio.google.com/u/0/) :** Best for small teams and freelancers reporting on Google Ads, GA4, and Sheets data at no cost
7. **[Zoho Analytics](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/) :** Best for small and midsize businesses that want AI-assisted reporting without enterprise pricing
8. **[ThoughtSpot](https://www.thoughtspot.com/) :** Best for teams that want to type a question and get a chart without building a dashboard first
9. **[Qlik Sense](https://www.qlik.com/us/products/qlik-sense) :** Best for analysts exploring relationships across multiple connected datasets
10. **[Klipfolio](https://www.klipfolio.com/) :** Best for semi-technical teams building custom KPI dashboards with their own formulas
11. **[AgencyAnalytics](https://agencyanalytics.com/) :** Best for marketing agencies tracking SEO and PPC performance across many clients
12. **[DashThis](https://dashthis.com/) :** Best for small teams that want a template-based marketing dashboard without a learning curve
13. **[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) :** Best for quick, one-off summaries of data you paste directly into the chat
14. **[Claude](https://claude.ai/) :** Best for teams drafting long reports who want a single pass that summarizes large inputs without losing context
15. **[Notion AI](https://www.notion.so/product/ai) :** Best for teams that already track projects in Notion and want reports drafted alongside existing docs
16. **[Prezent](https://www.prezent.ai/) :** Best for enterprise teams turning data insights into branded, presentation-ready decks


## How I researched and tested these AI reporting tools


I went through documentation, product walkthroughs, and user reviews for every platform on this list.


For the tools I had direct access to, I used mock sales and marketing datasets to build a dashboard from raw data, generate a written summary report, and set up a report to run on a recurring basis. Then, I checked how much manual cleanup those outputs needed before they were ready to share.


**Here's what I considered:**


- **Dashboard clarity:** How easy each tool made it to turn raw numbers into a chart or dashboard a non-analyst could read at a glance
- **Report writing quality:** Whether the written summary explained what the numbers meant, or just restated them
- **Setup and data connections:** How much manual work it took to move from a spreadsheet or database to a finished output
- **Automation and scheduling:** Whether a report could rerun on a recurring basis without rebuilding it from scratch
- **Value at each price point:** What the free or entry-level plan actually unlocked versus what required an upgrade


The clearest split I found was between tools that build a chart and stop there, and the handful that also write up what the chart actually means.

## 1. Tableau: Best for enterprise visualization and analytics


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Tableau](https://www.tableau.com/) is a[business intelligence platform](https://julius.ai/articles/best-bi-tool) that turns connected data into interactive dashboards and visual reports.
- **Best for:** Enterprise teams that need governed, interactive dashboards spanning many departments and data sources


To see how Tableau handled a reporting task, I connected a mock sales dataset and asked Tableau Agent to break down revenue by region in plain English.


It generated a chart for me in under a minute. **Asking a follow-up question adjusted the same view** , so I didn't have to rebuild it from scratch.


Building a calculated field to compare year-over-year growth meant writing a level-of-detail expression, and I had to check the help docs to get the syntax right.


### Key features


- **Tableau Agent:** Generates charts and calculations from natural language questions typed into the interface.
- **Data connectors:** Connects to spreadsheets, cloud databases, and enterprise warehouses like Snowflake and BigQuery.
- **Tableau Pulse:** Sends automated metric alerts and plain-language explanations when tracked[KPIs](https://julius.ai/articles/kpi-dashboard) change.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Natural language querying through Tableau Agent speeds up building a first chart Calculated fields and advanced filters have a real learning curve for new users


A wide range of data connectors covers spreadsheets and major cloud warehouses Refreshing dashboards built on large datasets can take noticeably longer


Automated anomaly and trend alerts through Tableau Pulse flag changes without opening a dashboard


### What users say


**Pro:** "Tableau is a highly effective tool for data analysis and creating interactive, insightful dashboards. It offers an intuitive and easy-to-use interface that makes data visualization and analysis straightforward." (Komal S.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/tableau/reviews/tableau-review-12321101) )


**Con:** "Making an efficient dashboard demands selecting the right metrics and the appropriate ways to visualize data. Poorly organized source data may cause the necessity to spend extra time preparing the data for further presentation. Updating dashboards is not easy if the business requirements are often changing." (Priyanshu R.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/tableau/reviews/tableau-review-13340689) )


### Pricing


Tableau starts at **[$75 per user per month](https://www.tableau.com/pricing)** for a Creator license.


### Bottom line


Tableau's MCP Server lets AI agents like Claude or ChatGPT query governed Tableau data directly, though the depth of access can depend on which Tableau product and plan you're using. If the learning curve here feels like more than you want to take on, Julius might be a better fit for building an analysis without touching calculated fields.


## 2. Power BI: Best for Microsoft-ecosystem reporting


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Power BI](https://powerbi.microsoft.com/) is a business analytics platform that turns connected data into reports and dashboards inside Microsoft's ecosystem.
- **Best for:** Teams already working in Excel, SharePoint, or Dynamics 365 who want reporting built into daily tools


Power BI leans hard on Microsoft integration, so I wanted to see how it handled data already sitting in Excel.


I dropped a mock sales spreadsheet in and asked Copilot to summarize monthly revenue trends. It wrote the DAX measure on its own and **handed back a written summary next to the chart** , saving me a trip to the formula bar.


A second filter for regional comparisons tripped it up, so I had to dig through Microsoft's documentation to fix the DAX syntax myself.


### Key features


- **Copilot integration:** Generates DAX formulas, report summaries, and narrative explanations from natural language prompts.
- **Key Influencers visual:** Identifies which variables in a dataset most strongly affect a chosen metric.
- **Microsoft 365 connectivity:** Pulls data directly from Excel, SharePoint, and Dynamics 365 without manual export steps.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Native Excel integration makes it straightforward to pull in existing spreadsheets and datasets DAX formulas and data modeling concepts have a steep learning curve for beginners


Copilot-generated DAX formulas cut down on manually writing complex measures The interface gets harder to navigate with large datasets or many visualizations


Key Influencers surfaces which variables actually drive a metric without manual segmentation


### What users say


**Pro:** "I like Power BI because it makes data analysis and reporting more visual and easier to understand. I find it useful for turning data into interactive reports and dashboards, while the integration with Excel makes it convenient to work with existing datasets." (Madhav K.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/microsoft-microsoft-power-bi/reviews/microsoft-power-bi-review-13347821) )


**Con:** "I find the learning curve for beginners challenging. I struggle with advanced features, DAX formulas, and data modeling concepts. The interface can also feel complex when working with large datasets or many visualizations." (Mansi S.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/microsoft-microsoft-power-bi/reviews/microsoft-power-bi-review-13323224) )


### Pricing


Power BI starts at **[$14 per user per month](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/#Pricing)** .


### Bottom line


Power BI's integration with Microsoft Fabric connects it directly to enterprise data engineering pipelines. If your team doesn't already work in Microsoft's ecosystem, Domo could be worth a look for real-time dashboards pulling from many sources.


## 3. Domo: Best for real-time operational dashboards


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Domo](https://www.domo.com/) is a cloud-based business intelligence platform that pulls data from many connected sources into live dashboards.
- **Best for:** Operations teams that need continuously updating dashboards pulled from many connected sources


Domo pulls data from many different sources into one dashboard, so I linked two mock datasets, sales and marketing spend, to see how fast I could merge them into a single view.


**I had the initial dashboard together in a few clicks** , and I set a real-time alert for a sales dip that fired right on cue.


I ran into trouble building a second more detailed dashboard, since dragging and resizing several widgets became fiddly once I had more than a handful of charts running.


### Key features


- **Data connectors:** Pulls data from marketing platforms, databases, and cloud systems through a wide range of pre-built connectors.
- **Real-time alerts:** Notifies users through Slack, email, or push notification when a tracked metric crosses a set threshold.
- **Mobile dashboards:** Displays dashboards in a mobile-optimized view for checking metrics away from a desktop.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Centralizing many data sources into one dashboard cuts down on switching between tools to check different metrics Advanced reporting and custom dashboard setup have a real learning curve at first


Real-time alerts flag threshold changes without needing to check a dashboard manually Configuring more detailed dashboards with several widgets takes noticeably more time than simpler ones


Mobile-friendly dashboards make it easy to check metrics away from a desktop


### What users say


**Pro:** "I like that Domo brings data from multiple sources into one easy-to-use dashboard, making it faster to monitor performance and share clear insights with the team." (Verified User in Consumer Services,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/domo/reviews/domo-review-13364237) )


**Con:** "There is a learning curve when getting started, especially for advanced features and custom dashboards. Some reports can also take time to configure, but the platform becomes much easier to use with the experience." (Dakare D.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/domo/reviews/domo-review-13239159) )


### Pricing


Domo offers **[usage-based pricing](https://www.domo.com/pricing)** .


### Bottom line


Domo's Agent Catalyst framework lets teams build custom AI agents that trigger business processes on their own. If a live ops dashboard isn't the priority and a written report matters more, Whatagraph could be worth a look for prompt-built client reports.


## 4. Julius: Best for analysis paired with a written report


- **Type:** Both
- **What it does:**[Julius](https://julius.ai/) is an AI data analysis tool built around its AI Report Generator, which turns a spreadsheet, connected database, or a described need into a structured report.
- **Best for:** Marketers and analysts who want a computed report built from a spreadsheet or connected database in one step


We built[Julius' AI Report Generator](https://julius.ai/home/ai-report-generator) to compute every number in a report through real code before writing any narrative.


Give it a spreadsheet, a connected database, or a plain description of what you need, and Julius **runs the analysis first, then writes the report around the results** . Scheduled Runs can rerun that same analysis on a schedule, so a recurring report starts from current data each time.


The report can only analyze the data it's given, so gaps or errors in the source file carry straight through into the finished report.


### Key features


- **AI Report Generator:** Runs code against uploaded files or connected data, then writes a structured report with charts and a narrative around the results.
- **Scheduled Runs:** Reruns a report's analysis on a recurring basis so regular reports start from current data.
- **Data connectors:** Connects to databases and cloud warehouses, or works directly from an uploaded spreadsheet, CSV, or PDF.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Runs real code against the data before writing anything, so every chart traces back to a computed result Scheduled Runs are capped on lower-tier plans, so teams running frequent recurring reports may need a higher tier


Scheduled Runs reruns the analysis, so a recurring report starts from current data each time Well-structured, clearly labeled data produces the most reliable results, so messy spreadsheets may need cleanup first


Works from an uploaded file or a plain-English description, so no clean dataset needs to be ready in advance


### What users say


**Pro:** “If you spend more than 2 hours a week working with data, Julius AI will save you time. Start with the free plan. You’ll know within a week if it fits your workflow. For most non-technical users, it’s a no-brainer.” (Fahim Joharder,[Fahim AI](https://www.fahimai.com/julius-ai) independent Julius review)


**Con:** “Not gonna lie, the first time I uploaded a messy CSV with empty values, the results were off. AI can help identify outliers and handle empty values. But you still need to clean your raw data first.” (Fahim Joharder,[Fahim AI](https://www.fahimai.com/julius-ai) independent Julius review)


### Pricing


Julius starts at **[$16 per month](https://julius.ai/pricing)** .


### Bottom line


Julius carries SOC 2 Type II compliance for teams reporting on sensitive business data. If dashboard-style visual monitoring matters more than a written narrative, Tableau is likely the better starting point for that.


## 5. Whatagraph: Best for prompt-built agency reports


- **Type:** Report generator
- **What it does:**[Whatagraph](https://whatagraph.com/) is a marketing reporting platform that generates full client reports from a text prompt using its Whatagraph IQ feature.
- **Best for:** Marketing agencies that need full client reports built from campaign data without manually laying out each one


Whatagraph is built around generating a full report from a prompt, so I described a marketing report covering three campaigns and let Whatagraph IQ take it from there.


**It pulled in the connected ad accounts and returned a formatted report** with widgets and charts already laid out, which saved me from building each section by hand.


I tried uploading a screenshot of a client's brand guidelines next, and the color palette carried over automatically, though the font it picked didn't quite match what I'd uploaded.


### Key features


- **Whatagraph IQ:** Builds a full report with widgets, layout, and styling from a text prompt using connected data sources.
- **IQ Chat:** Answers follow-up questions about a report's data in a conversational format.
- **Managed integrations:** Connects to 55+ marketing platforms without requiring manual API setup.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Whatagraph IQ builds a complete, styled report from a single prompt instead of a blank template Auto-detected branding from an uploaded screenshot doesn't always match fonts exactly


IQ Chat answers follow-up questions about the data without rebuilding the report Reports lean heavily on connected marketing platforms, so non-marketing data sources have less native support


55+ managed integrations cut down on manual setup for common ad and[analytics platforms](https://julius.ai/articles/analytics-and-reporting-tools)


### What users say


**Pro:** "I really appreciate Whatagraph's clean and easy-to-customize interface, which has made it quite intuitive for our small analytics team. The easy report sharing feature has been a big plus for us." (Anna A.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/whatagraph/reviews/whatagraph-review-13202214) )


**Con:** "The only thing I don't like about Whatagraph is that sometimes the website/server is slow when I need to download multiple reports." (Alyssa A.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/whatagraph/reviews/whatagraph-review-12569787) )


### Pricing


Whatagraph starts at **[$812 per month](https://whatagraph.com/pricing)** .


### Bottom line


Whatagraph can flag when a client's campaign moves outside a set budget, alerting Slack or email. If the reporting need leans more toward a live dashboard than a styled report, Domo might make more sense for real-time operational monitoring.


## 6. Data Studio: Best for free Google-data reporting


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Data Studio](https://datastudio.google.com/u/0/) is a free reporting tool that turns connected Google data into dashboards and shareable reports.
- **Best for:** Small teams and freelancers reporting on Google Ads, GA4, and Sheets data at no cost


Data Studio is built around native Google integrations, so I connected a mock Google Ads account to see how fast a report would come together.


**I had a dashboard live within minutes** , and sharing it required nothing more than sending a link. Pulling in a non-Google data source meant installing a community connector from the marketplace first, since native support stays limited to Google's own products.


### Key features


- **Native Google integrations:** Connects directly to Google Ads, Analytics, and Sheets without manual exports.
- **Community connectors:** Extends data access to non-Google sources through third-party marketplace connectors.
- **Template gallery:** Provides pre-built report templates for common categories like marketing and ecommerce.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Free access removes cost as a barrier for small teams and freelancers Native support outside Google's own products depends on third-party community connectors


Native Google integrations cut out manual data exports entirely Formatting and customization options are more limited than dedicated visualization tools


A large template library speeds up building a first report


### What users say


**Pro:** “It’s easy to build reports without needing anything advanced. Drag-and-drop charts, simple layout tools, and quick data connections make it really fast to get a dashboard live.” (Kelley G.,[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/190616/Data-Studio/#Capterra___7054023/) )


**Con:** “Looker Studio can feel limited when it comes to more advanced data modeling and complex calculations. Performance may slow down with larger datasets, and some connectors can be unreliable or end up requiring workarounds.” (Candy N.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/looker-studio/reviews/looker-studio-review-12286035) )


### Pricing


Data Studio is **free** .


### Bottom line


Data Studio's April 2026 rebrand folded in BigQuery conversational agents and Colab-built data apps as part of the same free workspace. If your reporting draws mainly from non-Google sources, Zoho Analytics might be a better fit for broad third-party integrations.


## 7. Zoho Analytics: Best for budget-friendly AI reporting


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Zoho Analytics](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/) is a self-service BI platform that turns spreadsheets and databases into dashboards with AI-assisted analysis.
- **Best for:** Small and midsize businesses that want AI-assisted reporting without enterprise pricing


Zoho Analytics markets itself as budget-friendly with a light setup, so I tested a mock sales dataset to see whether that ease came at the cost of real analytical depth.


I built a dashboard and asked its AI assistant, Zia, to summarize sales trends, **and it gave a plain-English answer beside the chart** . I found chart formatting options were fairly basic next to dedicated visualization tools like Tableau.


### Key features


- **Zia AI assistant:** Answers plain-language questions about connected data and summarizes trends.
- **Broad integrations:** Connects to a wide range of business apps, spreadsheets, and databases.
- **Report scheduling:** Sends dashboards and reports to email or Slack on a recurring basis.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Approachable pricing makes AI-assisted reporting accessible for smaller teams Chart formatting options stay fairly basic next to dedicated visualization tools


Zia answers plain-language questions about the data without writing a query Some advanced features need a higher-tier plan to unlock


Broad integrations cover common business apps beyond spreadsheets


### What users say


**Pro:** "Excellent tool for all reporting purposes. We use Zoho Analytics to sync up our data with Zoho Books, and then to create our entire reporting system out of it." (Abhinandan J.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoho-analytics/reviews/zoho-analytics-review-12722454) )


**Con:** "I've experienced slow performance when working with large datasets, and the customization options feel limited compared to competitors. Data integration has also been challenging, the interface comes across as clunky, and customer support has been slow to respond." (Sushank M.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoho-analytics/reviews/zoho-analytics-review-12599628) )


### Pricing


Zoho Analytics starts at **[$24 per month](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html)** for the Cloud plan.


### Bottom line


Zoho Analytics ties into the broader Zoho software suite for teams already running CRM or finance tools on Zoho. If budget isn't the deciding factor, ThoughtSpot is worth a look for a more search-driven way into the same data.


## 8. ThoughtSpot: Best for search-driven analytics


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[ThoughtSpot](https://www.thoughtspot.com/) is a search-driven analytics platform that returns charts and answers from typed questions without a built dashboard.
- **Best for:** Teams that want to type a question and get a chart without building a dashboard first


I wanted to see how ThoughtSpot handled a question with no dashboard built behind it yet, since it skips the usual dashboard-building step and lets you ask directly.


I typed a plain question about mock regional sales, **and its AI agent, Spotter, returned a chart along with a few related trends worth checking** . Getting a reliable answer on a second, more specific question depended on how cleanly the underlying data had been modeled beforehand.


### Key features


- **Spotter AI agent:** Answers typed questions with a chart and related trends without a pre-built dashboard.
- **Anomaly detection:** Flags unusual patterns in connected data automatically.
- **Embedded analytics:** Lets other applications embed ThoughtSpot's search and visualization directly.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


Typing a question returns a chart without building a dashboard first Reliable answers depend on how cleanly the underlying data was modeled


Spotter returns related trends alongside the direct answer to a question Embedded analytics setup can require technical help to configure


Anomaly detection flags unusual patterns without a manual review


### What users say


**Pro:** "I really like the Conversational AI, Agentic features, and the Spotter functionality of ThoughtSpot. They provide additional insights and explanations, making the platform thorough, easy to access, and ubiquitous. The value comes in speed, clarity, and broader access to insights, as it reduces the friction between a business question and a usable answer." (Farid V.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/thoughtspot/reviews/thoughtspot-review-12592167) )


**Con:** "The formulas don't use SQL or Excel-style formatting, so they're difficult to build, understand, and troubleshoot. Also, for a dashboard to include filters, the data has to be created as a model rather than pulled directly from the source table. That's frustrating because it adds an extra step to what should be a straightforward setup." (Isabelle N.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/thoughtspot/reviews/thoughtspot-review-12214025) )


### Pricing


ThoughtSpot starts at **[$25 per user per month](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing)** . Spotter and other AI features require the Pro plan or higher.


### Bottom line


ThoughtSpot's embedded analytics lets other software products build its search interface directly into their own applications. If clean data modeling upfront isn't realistic for your team, Data Studio could be a simpler starting point for free, low-maintenance reporting.


## 9. Qlik Sense: Best for associative data exploration


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Qlik Sense](https://www.qlik.com/us/products/qlik-sense) is an enterprise BI platform built around an associative data engine that links every field in a connected dataset.
- **Best for:** Analysts exploring relationships across multiple connected datasets


I wanted to see how Qlik Sense's associative engine handled a dataset with no predefined query path, so I clicked through a mock product catalog to explore it. Clicking one field highlighted every related value across the rest of the dataset, and I found a pattern in returns by category I wouldn't have thought to filter for directly. Getting comfortable navigating that way took longer than building a chart in a standard dashboard tool.


### Key features


- **Associative engine:** Links every field in a dataset so selecting one value highlights related data across all connected tables.
- **AI-suggested insights:** Surfaces correlations and patterns the person exploring the data might not have queried directly.
- **Enterprise governance:** Manages data access and permissions across large teams and departments.


### Pros and cons


**✅ Pros** **❌ Cons**


The associative engine surfaces related data without writing a query Navigating associative exploration has a real learning curve for new users


AI-suggested correlations can reveal patterns a manual filter would have missed Enterprise governance features add setup complexity smaller teams may not need


Clicking any field re-centers the whole view around it


### What users say


**Pro:** “It helps to consolidate data from all kinds of data sources with short loading time and allow interactions with 3rd party software to automate repetitive operations.” (Verified User in Wholesale,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/qlik-sense/reviews/qlik-sense-review-12385597) )


**Con:** “Sometimes there are loading issues, especially when business intelligence is running updates. It can be an issue, usually on Mondays, from morning into late afternoon, when all my data is pulling in at once. I feel like at times additional resources could be allocated.” (Terrance M.,[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/qlik-sense/reviews/qlik-sense-review-12263140) )


### Pricing


Qlik Sense starts at **[$300 per month](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing)** for 10 users.


### Bottom line


Qlik Sense's AI-suggested insights can flag a correlation before an analyst thinks to look for it. If associative exploration feels like more to learn than your team needs, Data Studio offers a simpler, free starting point instead.


## 10. Klipfolio: Best for custom KPI dashboards


- **Type:** BI dashboard
- **What it does:**[Klipfolio](https://www.klipfolio.com/) is a dashboard platform that turns connected data into KPI tracking views built around custom formulas.
- **Best for:** Semi-technical teams building custom KPI dashboards with their own formulas


I wanted to see how far Klipfolio's formula system could go without any spreadsheet background, so I combined two mock revenue sources into a single tracked metric.


**The dashboard updated as soon as I saved the formula** , and I could reference that same metric across other widgets right away. Getting the formula syntax right on my first attempt took a few tries, since it works more like a scripting language than a spreadsheet function.


### Key features


- **Custom formulas:** Builds calculated metrics from one or more connected data sources using a formula language.
- **Connector library:** Pulls data from over 100 marketing, sales, and finance platforms.
- **Flexible styling:** Adjusts dashboard layout, colors, and widget types beyond fixed templates.


### Pros and cons

## Which AI reporting tool should you choose?


The right pick comes down to whether you need a[live dashboard or a written report](https://julius.ai/articles/data-dashboards-vs-reports) , and which tools your team already uses.


**Choose Tableau if you:**


- Need a dashboard connecting spreadsheets, cloud warehouses, and enterprise data sources in one place
- Want conversational analytics that still supports building custom calculated fields for complex comparisons
- Want automated alerts sent straight to Slack when a tracked metric shifts


**Choose Power BI if you:**


- Already have reporting data spread across Excel, SharePoint, or Dynamics 365
- Want AI-generated DAX formulas and written narratives without building every measure by hand
- Need to know which variables are driving a metric without manually segmenting the data


**Choose Domo if you:**


- Are pulling from many disconnected sources and want them merged into one live view
- Need threshold-based alerts pushed to Slack, email, or mobile the moment a metric moves
- Want to build custom AI agents that trigger a business process directly from a dashboard


**Choose Julius if you:**


- Want a report built around numbers computed through real code, with the narrative written around them
- Need reporting to rerun on a schedule so a recurring report starts from current data every time
- Are starting from a plain description of what you need, even without a cleaned dataset ready


**Choose Whatagraph if you:**


- Manage reporting for multiple clients and want each report styled to match their brand automatically
- Want a full report built from a single prompt, with widgets and layout already assembled
- Have reporting that draws mainly from the marketing platforms already covered by its managed integrations

- Need free reporting on Google Ads, GA4, or Sheets data with no budget for a paid tool
- Want native integrations that skip manual exports from Google's own products
- Are comfortable adding a community connector for anything outside Google's ecosystem

- Need a search interface that can also embed inside another application

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best AI tool for reports?


Some of the best AI reporting tools include **Tableau, Power BI, and Julius** , depending on whether you need a live dashboard or a written report. Tableau and Power BI suit teams that want an interactive dashboard, while Julius computes the numbers first and writes the report around them. Whatagraph fits agencies reporting to multiple clients.


### What is an AI reporting tool?


An AI reporting tool is **software that turns raw data into a dashboard, chart, or written report using natural language** , without manual queries or spreadsheet formulas. You describe what you need or connect a data source, and the tool analyzes the data and builds the output automatically. Some tools also rerun reports on a schedule.


### Are AI reporting tools accurate?


**Yes, AI reporting tools can be accurate** , but the result depends on the quality of the connected or uploaded data. Tools that compute numbers through actual code tend to produce more reliable figures than tools that generate a written answer without running the calculation. Checking a report's underlying data before sharing it is worth doing.


### What's the difference between AI reporting tools and traditional BI tools?


The main difference is **setup** . Older BI workflows required a dashboard and data model built before anyone could explore the data. AI features in tools like Tableau and Power BI, plus AI-native tools like Julius, let you ask a question in plain language and get a chart back right away.


### Do AI reporting tools replace data analysts?


**No, AI reporting tools don't replace data analysts** , since someone still needs to judge whether a question was framed correctly and whether the output makes sense. What changes is the amount of manual report-building an analyst has to do by hand. Analysts can spend more time interpreting results and less time assembling charts.
